scope: Chrome 153 production-browser memory and speed recovery of the public MOV-to-AVI packet-copy route at its 191718419-byte published maximum

browser.name: Chrome
browser.memoryFormula: peak complete Chromium process-tree private memory during conversion - stable clean blank-Chromium process-tree private memory

rejectedBaseline.failure: All three runs exceeded the unchanged 250 MiB complete-browser limit, despite genuine repeatable output and cancellation cleanup.

acceptedTopology.directSave: Quota-preflighted synchronous browser-private stage followed by one backpressured 256 KiB copy to the selected destination; staging deleted on success, cancellation, write failure, or worker crash.
acceptedTopology.opfsTest: Existing synchronous OPFS writer without an additional final copy.

focusedProductionBrowserChecks.genuineSmallConversion: MOV to genuine AVI passed independent FFprobe, exact compressed packets, decoded-video equality, and complete native decode.
focusedProductionBrowserChecks.injectedFinalCopyWriteFailure: Error surfaced, at most one pending bounded write, partial destination removed, and no stage remained.
focusedProductionBrowserChecks.injectedWorkerCrash: Error surfaced, the OPFS stage and partial destination were removed, and the conversion worker restarted to ready.

speedDecision: For identical source and byte-identical output, the nine staged direct runs had a 4.37904-second median versus 47.365845 seconds for the rejected direct writer, a 10.82x median improvement. The accepted path lowered the observed worst complete-browser incremental private memory by 66.80859375 MiB.
limitations: The worst direct-save run left only 5.80859375 MiB of measured headroom on this Chrome version and machine, not a cross-machine guarantee. Browser-private staging temporarily consumes one output-sized amount of disk space before deletion.
